newsitem.title: PANAMA: Hutchison on target to run Panama ports.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison on target to run Panama ports.

text.p: A unit of Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa Ltd is on target with plans to start operating Panama's two main ports, a top government official said.
The company will install two mobile cranes at Cristobal Port, the Panama Canal's Atlantic Coast entrance, on March 1, National Port Authority Deputy General Director Ruben Reyna said.
"They will also repair two cranes there, in effect doubling the port's capacity" of slightly more than 100,000 cargo containers per year, he said.
At Balboa Port, the canal's Pacific coast entrance, the company will install cranes and construct cargo container patios. Balboa handles some 28,000 cargo containers a year.
The Panamanian government awarded the Hong Kong group the contract to operate the two ports upon a $22.2 million offer.
